about.title: About JalTaap
about.lead: JalTaap is a WhatsApp-first safety copilot for India's outdoor workers, such as construction workers and delivery riders. It turns weather forecasts into a plain-language heat plan, warns about waterlogged roads, plans whole crews' work and rest, and routes verified hazard and water-supply reports to the agency that owns them.
about.stat1: Several parts of Delhi crossed 46 °C on 22 May 2026.
about.stat2: Traffic Police flagged 169 waterlogging-prone hotspots in 2026.
about.stat3: The ILO projects India loses 5.8% of working hours to heat by 2030.
about.heatIntro: Each hour of the forecast gets one band, using wet-bulb temperature (heat plus humidity) and air temperature. The first rule that matches wins:
about.heatRed: wet-bulb at least 30 °C or temperature at least 44 °C
about.heatOrange: wet-bulb at least 28 °C or temperature at least 40 °C
about.heatYellow: wet-bulb at least 25 °C or temperature at least 37 °C
about.escalation1: Hot nights: when the night stays at or above 30 °C, the body cannot recover, so the band rises.
about.escalation2: Heat streaks: the third ORANGE day in a row raises the band.
about.escalation3: Personal profile: heavy work or health conditions shared in the chat can raise the band for that person.
about.floodFormula: risk = min(1, susceptibility × rain factor + antecedent bonus)
about.floodExplain: Susceptibility comes from how often a spot appears on official hotspot lists (underpasses score higher). The rain factor comes from forecast rain in the next 1 and 3 hours. The antecedent bonus is added after heavy rain in the last 24 hours.
about.floodLevels: The risk score maps to LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH or SEVERE. A spot becomes CONFIRMED when a verified photo report is within 300 m in the last 2 hours.
about.srcOpenMeteo: Weather forecasts and historical reanalysis: Open-Meteo.com, licensed CC BY 4.0.
about.srcOsm: Map data: © OpenStreetMap contributors, licensed ODbL.
about.srcMapAmazon: Map tiles and style: Amazon Location Service.
about.srcMapOfm: Map tiles and style: OpenFreeMap (OpenMapTiles schema).
about.srcHotspots: Waterlogging hotspots: public lists from Delhi Traffic Police and civic agencies, as reported in the news.
about.limit1: All weather values are modelled data, not readings from weather stations.
about.limit2: Hotspot lists change every year, so some waterlogging spots may be missing.
about.limit3: JalTaap is not an official warning service. Follow IMD and your state and city advisories.
about.team: Built by Team DevCore for Environmental Hacks (Heat & Water track).
about.tierFull: 36-cell heat grid, listed waterlogging hotspots with the owning agency (PWD, MCD, NDMC), cooling zones, the Delhi Jal Board for water problems, and replays.
about.tierCities: Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and every other million-plus city and state or UT capital: live heat, area rain risk and alerts. Researched waterlogging hotspots in 10 big cities; hospitals and drinking-water points from OpenStreetMap everywhere; reports go to each city's own bodies.
about.tierPoint: Send any place name or location pin: the personal hourly heat plan, crew plan and area rain risk work for that exact point.
about.featureCrew: Supervisors get an hour-by-hour roster for the whole crew: heavy work windows, staggered shade breaks so the site never stops, and litres of water to carry. Printable from the Crew plan page.
about.featureWater: Leaks, tanker no-shows, dry taps and dirty water, by photo or a plain message. Three independent reports from the same area, or a verified photo, put it on the map for the city's water board.
about.featureVoice: Send a voice note on WhatsApp or Telegram: Amazon Transcribe understands Hindi or Indian English, and Amazon Polly reads the reply back.
about.featureCedar: Cedar policies (AWS open source) decide officer actions: only the owning agency can act, only verified reports can be resolved, and disputed spots can be handed to another agency.
about.citiesChartAlt: Chart of dangerous heat days per city in 2026, split into days a 40 °C rule flags and days only humidity flags
about.srcCities: City centres: Open-Meteo Geocoding API. Agency names outside Delhi are starting values.
about.limit5: Outside Delhi there are no listed hotspots yet, so rain risk is for the area, not a specific underpass, and few cooling points are on record.
about.heroTitle1: Safe work in heat, rain and bad air,
about.heroTitle2: for every outdoor worker in India.
about.airBody: An India AQI estimate from modelled PM2.5 and PM10 (CPCB breakpoints) and the UV index (WHO categories). When the air is poor or the sun strong, the plan adds mask and head-cover advice.
about.proofTitle: city-days of humid danger that a 40 °C rule missed in 2026

problem.title: Heat warnings are city-wide and temperature-only. Workers need more.
problem.n1: Several parts of Delhi crossed 46 °C on 22 May 2026.
problem.n2: city-days in 2026 were dangerous by humidity alone, across 63 cities. A 40 °C rule never flagged them.
problem.n3: dangerous days in Kolkata in 2026. A 40 °C heatwave rule caught none of them.
problem.n4: of working hours India loses to heat by 2030.

simple.title: One look. One answer. Even if you can't read.
simple.body: The worker screen shows a single colour, a big picture and a few words. Every answer can be heard aloud in Hindi, and the most important button calls 112.
simple.p1: Tap Listen and the phone reads the plan aloud. Or send a voice note on WhatsApp.
simple.p2: Green, yellow, orange, red, always with an icon, never colour alone.
simple.p3: No app to install, no account. Just send a place name or a location pin.
simple.p4: A big red Call 112 button and first-aid steps when someone feels unwell.

features.title: Heat, rain, air and water. Hour by hour.
features.f1: Heat bands from wet-bulb and temperature for every hour, with the noon pause and the hours that are safe for heavy work.
features.f2: Voice notes are understood with Amazon Transcribe and answered with Amazon Polly.
features.f3: Listed Delhi underpasses and area rain risk everywhere else, at most one alert every 6 hours.
features.f4: A vision model checks each photo; verified pins reach the agency that owns the spot.
features.f5: Staggered rest groups so work never stops, and the litres of water to carry.
features.f6: Leaks, tanker no-shows and dry taps go to the water board once three people agree.
features.f7: An India AQI estimate and the UV index, with mask and head-cover advice when they matter. In October, Delhi's air becomes the bigger danger.

live.title: The dashboard behind every answer
live.body: Real forecast data for the next 48 hours. Hover or tap the chart for any hour.

how.title: From a question to a safe day, in seconds
how.body: Risk is computed by a tested engine, never guessed by the AI. The AI only talks.
how.step1: Type, send a pin or a voice note in Hindi, Hinglish or English on WhatsApp, Telegram or the web.
how.step2: Wet-bulb, hot nights, rain and air quality for your exact spot, from the same unit-tested Python every surface uses.
how.step3Title: A short answer, in your language
how.step3: At most six lines with the data time, read aloud if you want. Emergencies put Call 112 first.
how.step4: Verified reports go to the agency that owns the spot, with Cedar policies deciding who can close them.

proof.title: city-days of humid danger a 40 °C rule missed in 2026
proof.body: Across 63 cities from April to July 2026, JalTaap's wet-bulb rule flagged dangerous days that a temperature-only heatwave rule never would. Kolkata: 42 dangerous days, none caught by the 40 °C rule.
proof.caption: Modelled data (Open-Meteo reanalysis), one city-centre point per city, daytime 06:00–19:59 IST.

agency.title: Verified reports, routed to the right desk
agency.body: Officers see only their agency's queue, with photos, location and an AI action brief that cites real report ids.
agency.a1: Only the owning agency can act; only verified reports can be closed.
agency.a2: Disputed spots can be handed to another agency in one click.
agency.a3: City control rooms get a read-only view of every report.

aws.title: Built on AWS
aws.body: Serverless in Mumbai (ap-south-1), defined in one AWS SAM template.

faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: Yes. JalTaap uses free public weather data and runs on WhatsApp, Telegram and the web.
faq.q2: Do I need to read or type?
faq.a2: No. Send a voice note or a location pin, and tap Listen on the website to hear the answer.
faq.a3: Heat plans work anywhere in India. Delhi has full coverage. 62 more cities, every million-plus city and every state and UT capital, are on the live map with heat, rain, air and the nearest hospitals and water points.
faq.a4: No. It uses modelled forecast data. Always follow IMD and government advice, and call 112 in an emergency.
faq.q5: What do you store about me?
faq.a5: Only your language, a rough location (about 1 km), alerts you ask for and photos you send. Send STOP to delete everything.

final.title: Make today a safe day at work.
final.body: Check your area now, or plan the day for your whole crew.

landing.footerNote: Weather and air data are modelled forecasts, not station readings. Not an official warning service. In an emergency, call 112.

personal.title: Warnings for you, where you are
personal.body: JalTaap follows your location while you work and tells you before heat, rain or polluted air turns dangerous, adjusted to your age, health and the work you do.
personal.c1: Heavy work, age 60+, pregnancy, a long-term illness or being new to the heat: each makes the advice stricter, as health guidelines recommend.
personal.c2: Live location keeps the next 3 hours of heat, rain, air and sun fresh as you move across the city.
personal.c3: One clear warning when risk rises, one all-clear when it passes. On the web or on Telegram, with no spam.

unwell.title: Is someone unwell in the heat?
unwell.dangerSub: This can be heatstroke. Call 112, then do these steps while you wait:
unwell.s1: Move them to shade or a cool place
unwell.s5: Give water only if fully awake
unwell.s6: Stay with them until help comes
unwell.mildSub: Stop work and cool down. Watch them closely.
unwell.m1: Sit or lie down in the shade
unwell.m4: Cool the face and neck with water
unwell.m6: Not better in 30 minutes, or getting worse? Call 112
unwell.noHospital: No hospital on record within 30 km. Call 112.
unwell.notDiagnosis: This is first aid, not a diagnosis. When in doubt, call 112.

profile.title: About you
profile.body: Each one you tick makes heat advice one step stricter for you, as health guidelines recommend. Tick only what is true.

heavy_work.title: I do heavy physical work
heavy_work.body: Construction, loading, digging, carrying or pulling loads.

age_60_plus.title: I am 60 or older
age_60_plus.body: The body cools down more slowly with age.

pregnant.title: I am pregnant
pregnant.body: Heat puts extra strain on the body during pregnancy.

chronic_illness.title: I have a long-term illness
chronic_illness.body: Heart, lung or kidney disease, diabetes or high blood pressure.

not_acclimatised.title: I am new to this heat
not_acclimatised.body: Arrived in the last two weeks, or back after a long break.

notify.title: Phone notifications
notify.body: Get a notification when a new warning starts, even when you are on another page.

telegram.title: Warnings on Telegram, even with the app closed
telegram.s1: Open the JalTaap bot in Telegram and say hello.
telegram.s2: Tap 📎 → Location → Share My Live Location, and choose how long.
telegram.s3: JalTaap messages you only when the risk where you are changes.

privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.p1: Your profile and settings are saved only on this device.
privacy.p2: To get the forecast, only a rounded location (about 100 m) is sent. JalTaap does not store it.
privacy.p3: JalTaap never asks for your name, phone number or Aadhaar.
